memory_update.text: MKSI is a reference anchor for the node: broad vacuum, flow, gas delivery, power delivery, photonics, process-control, and specialty-chemistry exposure inside semiconductor manufacturing and electronics-packaging equipment.
AEIS is a reference anchor for precision power/plasma power delivery in wafer-fabrication equipment, especially advanced plasma processing applications.

UCTT is an underfollowed discovery-lane candidate with direct semiconductor capital equipment OEM exposure through critical subsystems, components, parts, ultra-high-purity cleaning, and analytical services.
ICHR is an underfollowed discovery-lane candidate with direct semiconductor capital equipment OEM exposure through gas and liquid delivery subsystems and components.

The strongest US-listed direct-exposure cluster for 'semicap subsystems inside OEM tools' appears to be MKSI, AEIS, UCTT, and ICHR; each sells critical subsystems or enabling modules into semiconductor equipment rather than selling complete process tools to fabs.

Need later-layer verification of actual customer names, revenue concentration, content per tool, sole-source status, qualification cycles, gross-margin durability, and whether AI-driven advanced-node and advanced-packaging capex flows through these subsystem suppliers.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the node 'semiconductor equipment subsystems embedded inside OEM fab tools.' The cleanest direct-exposure names are subsystem suppliers selling into wafer-fab-equipment OEMs rather than directly to fabs. MKS Instruments and Advanced Energy are higher-visibility reference/anchor names for vacuum, RF/plasma power, process control, and specialty chemistry. Ultra Clean and Ichor are more underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery-lane names with direct OEM dependency through critical subsystems, cleaning, gas delivery, and chemical/fluid delivery modules.
